blocks.prompt: 3. A particle moves along a straight line with acceleration \(a(t) = 12t - 36\) (m/s\(^2\)) and initial velocity \(v(0) = 30\) m/s. (a) Find the velocity function \(v(t)\).
blocks.explanation: Velocity from acceleration: integrate, then fix the constant with \(v(0) = 30\).
steps:
Given: \(a(t) = 12t - 36\), \(v(0) = 30\).
To find: \(v(t)\).
Method: \(v'(t) = a(t)\), so \(v\) is an antiderivative of \(a\); the initial velocity fixes the constant.

Integrate
\[v(t) = \int (12t - 36)\,dt\]
\[= 12\cdot\dfrac{t^{2}}{2} - 36t + c = 6t^{2} - 36t + c\]
Why: power rule, \(\int t\,dt = \frac{t^{2}}{2}\).

blocks.prompt: 3. A particle moves along a straight line with acceleration \(a(t) = 12t - 36\) (m/s\(^2\)) and initial velocity \(v(0) = 30\) m/s. (b) Find the displacement of the particle during the time period \(1 \le t \le 6\).
blocks.explanation:
Displacement is the integral of velocity over the interval, signs included.
Plan: integrate \(v(t)\) from 1 to 6.
steps:
Given: \(v(t) = 6t^{2} - 36t + 30\), interval \([1, 6]\).
To find: displacement \(s(6) - s(1)\).
Method: \(\int_{1}^{6} v(t)\,dt = s(6) - s(1)\) (Fundamental Theorem).

Put in the limits
\[F(6) = 432 - 648 + 180 = -36\]
\[F(1) = 2 - 18 + 30 = 14\]
\[\text{Displacement} = -36 - 14 = -50\]
Why: \(F(t) = 2t^{3} - 18t^{2} + 30t\); upper value minus lower value.

Meaning and check
\(-50\) m: the particle ends 50 m to the left of where it was at \(t = 1\). The split in part (c) gives \(-64 + 14 = -50\;\checkmark\).
blocks.final_answer: Displacement \(= -50\) m (50 m to the left).

blocks.prompt: 3. A particle moves along a straight line with acceleration \(a(t) = 12t - 36\) (m/s\(^2\)) and initial velocity \(v(0) = 30\) m/s. (c) Find the distance traveled during this time period.
blocks.explanation: Distance is \(\int |v|\,dt\): first find where \(v\) changes sign inside \([1, 6]\), then split.
steps:
Given: \(v(t) = 6t^{2} - 36t + 30\) on \([1, 6]\).
To find: total distance \(\int_{1}^{6}|v(t)|\,dt\).
Method: factorise \(v\), find its sign on each part, take \(-v\) where \(v < 0\).

Sign of \(v\)
\[v(t) = 6(t^{2} - 6t + 5) = 6(t - 1)(t - 5)\]
\(v \le 0\) on \([1, 5]\) and \(v \ge 0\) on \([5, 6]\).
Why: between the roots 1 and 5, \((t - 1) > 0\) and \((t - 5) < 0\); after 5 both are positive.

Add
\[\text{Distance} = 64 + 14 = 78\]
Why: 64 m to the left, then 14 m to the right.
